In World War Two, one American army unit went to war with balloons, speakers and paint.
They were called the Ghost Army. About eleven hundred men, many of them artists and designers.
Their job was to pretend to be someone else.
They inflated rubber tanks, trucks and cannons, that looked real from the air.
Speaker trucks blasted recordings of engines and soldiers, that could be heard miles away.
Radio operators sent fake messages, and soldiers spread fake gossip in French cafes.
Once, two French cyclists watched four soldiers lift a forty-ton tank. The soldiers just said, Americans are very strong.
The unit staged more than twenty deceptions, pulling German forces away from the real attacks.
Historians think they saved thousands of lives.
Their story stayed secret for fifty years. In 2022, they were finally awarded the Congressional Gold Medal.
